scripts.render-build: pnpm lint || echo '[render-build] lint reported issues (non-blocking for deploy; fix via CI/pre-commit)'; pnpm --filter @trading-app/shared build && pnpm --filter @trading-app/engine build && pnpm --filter @trading-app/backtest build && pnpm --filter @trading-app/server build && pnpm --filter desktop vite:build
scripts.//drain:strands: TRA-3541 — the WRITE half of check:strands. The board ruled on 2026-08-13 that hand-draining the blocked+empty recovery-strand cohort every 12h is not a fix; detection was owned and live, the DRAIN was owned by nobody. This does NOT re-implement the cohort predicate: it imports sweep() from check-blocked-empty.mjs and executes the RESTORE-PATCH pair that detector already derives, so the population written to is definitionally the population graded. Per row: POST comment, PATCH {"status":"todo"}, PATCH {"assigneeAgentId":returnOwnerAgentId} — in that order, because assignment is ONE-WAY (afterwards the comment and the status PATCH both 403). ⛔ NEVER `done` (destroys unrun work) and NEVER `blockedByIssueIds` (an empty write-key list reproduces the unroutable born-blocked state); both bans are enforced on the request BODY by gradeWriteBody(), not on the rendered report. Success is verified by RE-READ, never by the 2xx — a PATCH that returns 200 and does not stick reads as FAILED. ⛔ Repair is ASSIGNEE-SCOPED and rank does not lift it, so no single seat can drain the company: a row this seat cannot write is reported FOREIGN and drains from the OWNER's twin arm. Exit 0 VACUOUS (no drainable row existed — NOT a pass, nothing was exercised) / 0 DRAINED / 1 REMAINDER (ineligible or FOREIGN rows nobody is coming for) / 2 FAILED / 3 BLIND. Off-roster+unassigned rows and shape-2 rows are ACKNOWLEDGED: printed in full every fire, but they do not colour the exit, because both classes have a named owner and a daily red gets tuned out. The carve-out is a RULE (off-roster assignee), never an identifier list, so it expires by itself.
scripts.//check:routine-dispatch: TRA-2331 — grades the claim check:phantom-rest MAKES. That check clears a leaf as monitored on `active` + `enabled` + a FUTURE `nextRunAt`, and ⛔ `nextRunAt` IS A PROMISE, NOT A RECORD: it is recomputed from the cron and moves forward whether or not the fire ever dispatched, so a routine whose every dispatch is failing reads byte-for-byte identical to a healthy one. The discriminator is the run history. Reads the LIST route only — ⛔ that route OMITS the `recentRuns` key entirely (absent, not []) so `(r.recentRuns || []).length === 0` brands the whole company never-dispatched; it DOES carry `lastRun`, which is the tail verdict in one call. Exit 0 clean / 1 per-routine findings / 2 FLEET (spans the roster — ONE platform condition, do NOT file a ticket per routine) / 3 blind. Zero graded rows is BLIND, never clean. ⛔ TRA-3487 — a `failed` tail is now ATTRIBUTED against the durable owner-pause tape (`activity_log` agent.paused/agent.resumed/agent.terminated, read from the platform's Postgres) AT THE FAILURE INSTANT, splitting into OWNER_PAUSED / OWNER_TERMINATED / OWNER_STATE_UNKNOWN. All three stay findings but are HELD OUT of the FLEET test, because FLEET is a claim about the DISPATCHER and per TRA-2871 the usual TRUE cause of a roster-wide burst is that the OWNERS WERE PAUSED — the old banner asserted 'ONE platform condition' unconditionally and so reproduced the TRA-2867/2871 misdiagnosis twice a day. The banner now NAMES its subject, and a roster-wide pause prints an OWNER PAUSE BURST instead. ⛔ Attribution FAILS CLOSED: an unreadable tape, a coverage floor that does not reach the failure, or an `agent.updated` PATCH touching `status` (the platform logs the KEY, never the VALUE, and agent_config_revisions does not track `status` at all) each yield OWNER_STATE_UNKNOWN — never 'the owner was fine'. ⛔ Do NOT read the tape from /api/../activity: its `action` filter is SILENTLY IGNORED and limit=1000 returns 500 rows (~3.4h).
scripts.//check:carrier-dispatch: TRA-3529 — the NEXT link after check:routine-dispatch. That one grades the DISPATCH TAIL (did the fire produce a run?); this one grades what happens AFTER a successful dispatch: was anybody ever woken on the issue that run created? ⛔⛔ RUN `status` MEASURES ISSUE CLOSURE, NOT EXECUTION — a run sits at `issue_created` until its linked issue reaches a terminal status, and bb11cef4's run flipped to `completed` at the exact instant a sweep closed TRA-3513 BY HAND, no work in between. So `issue_created` (which is in the sibling's RUN_SUCCESS set, correctly, for its own subject) and `completed` both say nothing about whether the order was executed. The discriminator is `issue.startedAt` — the platform's record of a CHECKOUT — and ⛔ it is NOT `assigneeAgentId` (873 of 877 carriers carry one; the routine propagates it correctly) and ⛔ NOT `zero comments` (TRA-3529's stated discriminator, which HEALS WITHOUT A DISPATCH the moment a sweep closing the carrier writes a comment on the way past — a lagging proxy that fails toward CLEAN). ⛔⛔ TRAP: `lastRun.linkedIssue` on the LIST route serves SIX keys (id/identifier/priority/status/title/updatedAt) and `startedAt` IS NOT AMONG THEM, so reading it there brands all 197 carriers never-dispatched — this check FANS OUT to GET /api/issues/{id} and exits BLIND on an absent key. ⛔⛔ TRAP: routine status is NOT filtered — 163 of 197 carriers sit on ARCHIVED routines because a one-shot's own prose orders it to archive itself as step 1, so the `active`-only population that is right for the sibling check would hide 83% of carriers INCLUDING the self-archiving deploy trains that are the urgent case. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 SYSTEMIC with the subject NAMED / 3 blind. ⛔ A pile of findings on ONE assignee is that agent's QUEUE, not a dispatcher fault: measured 2026-08-13, the same agent's MANUALLY-created issues starved at 67% vs 62% for routine-spawned ones while every other assignee sat at ~0% regardless of origin, so the variable is queue depth and the founding cohort only looked routine-specific because it was selected routine-only. Only a spread across the roster leaves the dispatcher as the remaining subject. CARRIER_CANCELLED_UNWORKED (a deliberate retirement) stays a finding but is held OUT of the systemic test so retired routines cannot put a permanent floor under the verdict. ⛔ Grades ONE carrier per routine (the newest), so a worked newest carrier HIDES an abandoned older one — a NAMED blind spot, printed every run, not a silent cap.
scripts.//check:deploy-train-window: TRA-3533 — the residual of TRA-3529, and the OUTCOME leg its sibling structurally cannot reach. check:carrier-dispatch grades whether anybody was WOKEN on a routine's carrier; that is the right question about the queue and the wrong one about the deploy, because a carrier can be picked up promptly and the deploy still be refused, or abandoned entirely and the commit still be live off another path. This grades the OUTCOME: is the ordered commit an ancestor of the bytes bqb1 is executing? ⭐ THE POINT IS THAT IT DOES NOT REQUIRE THE CARRIER TO HAVE BEEN WORKED — a lateness check written INTO the carrier's own prose ("fail loudly if you read this past T") is structurally blind, because it only runs if somebody runs the carrier, which is the exact event whose absence IS the defect. ⛔ A deploy train must carry a machine-readable ```deploy-order block (commit/host/deadline); nothing on the board recorded WHAT was ordered or BY WHEN as data, which is why the 2026-08-13 disposition of TRA-3493/TRA-3511/TRA-3513 had to be a human re-derivation from prose. `deadline` MUST end in Z — crons are evaluated in ET and the windows are written in UTC, and a bare local time is REJECTED, never guessed. ⛔ SATISFIED means the commit is live NOW, not that it was live BY THE DEADLINE: the timing arm needs Render deploy history and reports UNREAD, never OK — on 08-13 both deploys were satisfied hours late by an unrelated path, which is exactly the case a bare pass would hide. ⛔ TWO EXIT CODES FOR TWO STATES, on purpose: 1 STRANDED (deadline passed, commit not live — the incident, the only code that should page) vs 4 UNGRADED (suspected trains carrying no block — a migration backlog). Folding them into one number buries the incident: the first live run flagged 18 suspected and 0 stranded. ⛔ The prose classifier is a HINT with known false positives (TRA-3413 says "if you find yourself about to redeploy bqb1, STOP"; TRA-3398 quotes an embargo) so it reports SUSPECTED, never "defective" — a grader over other people's artefacts fails toward convicting them. Opt out with `<!-- deploy-order: none -->`. ⛔ Default population is carriers fired in the last 7 days keyed on lastRun.triggeredAt, and the excluded count is PRINTED — the unfiltered first run flagged 53 settled July one-shots for lacking a field that did not exist when they were written. An unreadable triggeredAt is INCLUDED, never dropped. ⛔ Same NAMED blind spot as its sibling: ONE carrier per routine, the newest. Exit 0 clean / 1 STRANDED / 2 usage / 3 BLIND / 4 UNGRADED; precedence BLIND > STRANDED > UNGRADED > CLEAN. Live path proven both directions on TRA-3536 (a real fixture issue whose ordered commit is the SHA ALREADY LIVE, so obeying it is a strict no-op).
scripts.//check:spent-oneshot: TRA-3008 — the complement of check:routine-dispatch. That one grades the DISPATCH TAIL (did the last fire run?); this one grades the FORWARD PROMISE. ⛔ A DATE-PINNED ONE-SHOT CRON HAS NO YEAR FIELD, so after its single fire the scheduler re-arms it ~365d out and the routine keeps reading as live scheduled coverage on every census — a SPENT one-shot is indistinguishable from an ARMED one, and its last run can be perfectly `completed`, so a tail verdict cannot reach it. Finds an `active` routine with an `enabled` schedule trigger whose `nextRunAt` is beyond the horizon (default 120d — wider than any legitimate quarterly cadence). ⛔ ARCHIVING DOES NOT DISABLE THE TRIGGER (measured on c0ca474e: status archived, enabled still true, nextRunAt still 2027) so `status==='active'` is the discriminator, not `enabled` — and archiving IS the remedy. ⛔ The routines route returns a BARE ARRAY: the first run of this census read `body.routines`, matched nothing, and reported 0 against a company that had 8. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings with coverage intact / 2 COVERAGE_LOST (a routine whose only arms are spent) / 3 blind. Zero graded rows is BLIND, never clean. ⛔ TRA-3017 — this check is armed DAILY (routine efd820ff) under prose that says `file ONE issue on exit != 0`, and two coverage-lost rows CANNOT be repaired by the agent running it (routine writes 403 across the assignee boundary; e1b97e28's assignee has DEPARTED, so NO agent can archive it — it needs a BOARD re-home). Left alone the daily fire mints a duplicate issue for the same rows every morning until someone retires the checker. `scripts/spent-oneshot-acknowledged.json` (HAND-EDITED ONLY) suppresses the EXIT CODE and nothing else — acknowledged rows are still printed IN FULL every run, every entry must name a live `trackedBy` issue plus a `reason` or it is IGNORED, and each is pinned to the cron+nextRunAt of EVERY spent arm on the row so a re-arm expires the pin by itself. New verdict ACKNOWLEDGED_ONLY = exit 0 “file nothing”, which is NOT “coverage is intact”. An unreadable ledger degrades to ZERO acks (more filing), never blanket suppression.
scripts.//check:data-dir: TRA-2603 — frozen-baseline ratchet on the unguarded `process.env.DATA_DIR ?? join(__dirname,'..','data')` literal. `??` does not guard a present-but-BLANK value; resolveDataDir() adds the .trim(). Baseline is now ZERO known copies — TRA-2604 migrated all 38 — so any non-zero count is a REGRESSION, not backlog. HAND-EDITED ONLY; never regenerate it from the tree. Exit 1 drift / 2 instrument broken / 3 blind.
scripts.//check:continuity: TRA-2634 — grade the level-continuity detector against the REAL stored report archive (both directions, every run) and cross-tab it against the deployed r>=2 session-move rule. Control rows are SCOPED PER BOX and only this HOST's are graded, so run BOTH: `pnpm check:continuity` (bqb1) and `HOST=http://localhost:4242 pnpm check:continuity`. Build @trading-app/shared first — it imports dist. Exit 0 pass / 1 control failed / 3 BLIND, and 3 IS A HOLD.
scripts.//check:tra2399-controls: TRA-2399 AC3, END TO END: drives the real CLI over a real socket against a POPULATED book and an EMPTY one, and asserts exit 0 vs exit 4. Needs `pnpm build` first (it computes both payloads with the real gate out of dist/), which is why it is a named step and NOT in pretest — see the header of the script.
scripts.//tra2420:attribute: TRA-2420 — rank DATA_DIR's per-trading-day GROWTH by writer off /api/health/storage/detail (ADMIN-gated since TRA-2599, so this needs TRADINGAI_ADMIN_TOKEN or --token=). Exits 2 NOT_DEPLOYED until the deploy carrying the `usage` block lands, which is the only answer live can give before then — hence the paired controls. Exit 5 NO_TOKEN is a MISSING/REJECTED token, deliberately not folded into 3 BLIND: BLIND reads as 'the box is down' and would send you to Render instead of to your shell.
scripts.//check:pnl-lag: TRA-2630 AC3 — the T+1 options-credit lag regression guard (TRA-2629). Live-pull only: the defect is a DURABILITY seam, so an in-memory round trip passes while prod is broken. Partitions mode:live (exit 1, escalate) from demo (exit 2) and fails CLOSED to BLIND (exit 3) rather than reporting a green it could not measure. Exit 4 = LIVE CREDIT SHORTFALL (TRA-2635/TRA-2658), a SEPARATE axis that outranks demo lag on the exit code only — the `TRA-2630 AC2` delta verdict always prints ABOVE it and is what AC2 is graded on. AC2 is a DELTA (no NEW lag session on/after the fix-deploy date), never an absolute: the 18 pre-fix rows cannot clear retroactively.
scripts.//check:fix-live: TRA-2644 — 'is MY fix in the bytes being executed', which check:deploy-drift CANNOT answer. Ancestry of --commit against the live SHA, NOT drift: drift measures the whole company's merge rate against one box, so it is routinely non-zero on a weekday and a grading gate keyed to it never opens. Requires --commit (no default: a default is how a grader confirms the wrong fix). --window-start=<ISO> adds the arm a point-in-time SHA read cannot have — every build that held `live` across the window must contain the commit, because a rollback mid-session makes that session's EOD row a mixture of two writers. Exit 0 PRESENT / 1 ABSENT / 2 CONTAMINATED (window spans a build without the fix) / 3 BLIND. Fails closed: a SHALLOW checkout cannot distinguish 'not an ancestor' from 'unanswerable', so an unknown SHA exits BLIND, never ABSENT.
scripts.pretest: node scripts/check-stale-js.mjs && node scripts/check-data-dir.mjs && node scripts/check-cycles.mjs && node --test scripts/lib/render-boot-set.test.mjs && node --test scripts/lib/auth-secret-predicate.test.mjs && node --test scripts/lib/tra2399-live-instrument-grade.test.mjs && node scripts/tra2387-auth-secret-gate-check.mjs && node scripts/check-theo-arb.mjs --selftest && node scripts/check-tra3010-gate-a-selftest.mjs && node scripts/tra2631-provenance-stamp-check-selftest.mjs && node scripts/check-snapshot-persist.mjs --selftest && pnpm --filter @trading-app/shared build && pnpm --filter @trading-app/engine build && pnpm --filter @trading-app/backtest build

pnpm.//: TRA-1052 — .npmrc sets approve-builds=false, so pnpm skips dependency install/build scripts unless allowlisted here. better-sqlite3 is a native module that relies on prebuild-install (an install script) to fetch its prebuilt binary; WITHOUT this entry the binary is silently absent. TRA-1681 — this comment used to claim the server then 'crashes on require'. IT DOES NOT, and that wrong sentence is why the real risk looked self-announcing for months: sqlite.ts CATCHES the missing module, getStateDb() returns null, every caller falls back to in-memory, and the box boots and serves normally with the agent-spend cap NO LONGER DURABLE across restarts. The only signal is one log line, on a host that exposes no logs to a grader. `GET /api/health/durability` is now the readable verdict, and DURABILITY_POLICY=refuse is what makes it stop a boot. Listed explicitly so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on Render fetches the prebuilt .node (no compilation, so no render-build OOM regression — TRA-1037/1038).
